subject: Acme — discrepancy in November usage (token counts)
messages:
From: Laura Green <accounts-payable@acme.corp>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@acme.corp>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected overage on November invoice — token counts don't match

Hi Stephanie,

We received invoice #AC-2025-11 this morning and our accounts team flagged a large overage. The invoice shows 210,452 tokens billed for the period Nov 1–15. Our internal metering (sidecar proxy and client logs) reports 183,770 tokens for the same timeframe.

Attached is our export (Acme_Billing_Nov.csv) — we've highlighted the per-day totals. Can you look into why Redwood's token count is ~26k higher? We're trying to reconcile ahead of payment.

Questions we have:
- Can you provide a per-day, per-model token breakdown?
- Do you count assistant-only or system prompt tokens differently?
- Do retries / streaming partials get double-counted?

We'd appreciate a quick run-down and any adjustments if Redwood billing is incorrect.

Thanks,
Laura Green
Accounts Payable
Acme Corp
attachments: Acme_Billing_Nov.csv (csv)

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Green <accounts-payable@acme.corp>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 12:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on November invoice — token counts don't match

Hi Laura — thanks for the note and the export. I’ve looped in Marissa from billing and Diego from infra to triage.

Quick answers: we’ll produce a per-day, per-model token breakdown and a raw request-id level CSV. We also need a few sample request IDs or timestamps from your side for cross-checking (if possible).

Action plan:
- Diego will pull the relevant server-side logs and render a per-request breakdown (tokens: prompt, completion, total).
- Marissa will evaluate whether a provisional credit is appropriate while we investigate.
- I’ll follow up with a consolidated CSV and a proposal for an invoice adjustment by EOD Monday Nov 17.

Can you send 3–5 example timestamps (UTC) for requests you’re calling out? If not, we’ll proceed with our logs and flag any clear duplicates / retries.

Sorry for the trouble — we’ll get this sorted.

Sincerely,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Manager | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 12:27:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acme overage - quick triage

Marissa / Diego — forwarding Acme's note. High level: customer shows ~183.8k tokens, our invoice = 210.4k. They attached CSV.

Marissa — can we provisionally apply a credit if our logs show retries/duplicate billing? I don’t want collection held up.
Diego — can you pull request-level logs for Nov 1–15 for Acme (api_key id: acct_acme_01) and flag sessions with identical payloads or retries? If you can, please include model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, request_id, timestamp.

If we can get a per-request CSV we can reconcile quickly.

Thanks — S.

Onward,
Stephanie

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 02:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme overage - quick triage

Stephanie / Marissa — initial findings attached (redwood_logs_acme_20251115-18.csv). Summary of what I see:

- For Nov 11–16 there are ~26k tokens worth of requests that correspond to duplicated request_ids. These appear to be the result of Acme's client retrying on a proxy 502/504 around 2025-11-16 02:05–02:20 UTC (we have status 200 for both attempts).
- Many of the duplicated requests are streaming responses where the client re-sent the same payload. Our usage pipeline counts tokens per successful completion; however, when identical requests are received twice and both complete, both are billed.
- A small subset (~1200 tokens) is due to system prompt being longer than our default tokenization estimates for that model; that affects prompt_token counts.

Recommendation: provide a per-request export to Acme showing both attempts and offer a one-time credit for duplicate completions resulting from their retries. The duplicated completions sum to 25,982 tokens. At their current per-token rate ($0.012/1k tokens for the model used), that’s ~$311.78.

Next steps I can take: format and deliver the per-request CSV (filtered to Nov 11–16) and mark duplicated request_ids. I also flagged the incident #INC-2025-11-16-proxy-retries in our internal tracker.

Diego
Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_logs_acme_20251115-18.csv (csv)

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Green <accounts-payable@acme.corp>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@acme.corp>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on November invoice — token counts don't match

Hi Laura — thanks again for the export and patience. We completed our investigation and attached a detailed per-request breakdown (redwood_usage_breakdown_Acme_Nov15-18.csv). Key findings: 

1) Duplicate completions due to client retries: 25,982 tokens — these are identical request payloads that completed twice after clients retried when they saw intermediary proxy 5xxs.
2) Tokenization delta: ~1,670 tokens difference due to system prompt tokenization edge-cases on the model used (we’ve annotated those rows).

Total delta explained: 25,982 + 1,670 = 27,652 tokens, which matches the discrepancy on the invoice.

Proposed resolution:
- We’ll apply a one-time credit for the duplicate completions equivalent to 25,982 tokens at your contracted rate, which equals $312 (rounded to nearest dollar). This credit will be applied to your Nov invoice and reflected on the Dec statement.
- Tokenization differences (1,670 tokens) are within expected tokenization variance, but we’ve annotated the examples so your engineering team can adjust prompts if desired.

Attached: redwood_usage_breakdown_Acme_Nov15-18.csv (per-request: timestamp, request_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, note)

If that works for you we’ll issue the credit and update the invoice status. Also, for visibility we captured the proxy-retry incident in our tracker (https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-11-16-proxy-retries) and added recommendations for client-side idempotency keys to avoid double billing on retries.

Would you like a 30-minute call to walk through the CSV?

Sincerely,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Manager | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_usage_breakdown_Acme_Nov15-18.csv (csv)

On a tax/VAT note (from Marissa): credits are applied net of VAT — we will reflect the credit on the invoice line item and the VAT will adjust accordingly. If you need a formal credit memo for local tax teams let me know and we can generate one.

From: Laura Green <accounts-payable@acme.corp>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@acme.corp>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on November invoice — token counts don't match

Stephanie — thank you, and thanks Diego and Marissa for the fast turnaround. The CSV aligns with our logs; the duplicates are visible on our side too (we were seeing 502s from our proxy and retried). The proposed $312 credit is acceptable.

Please apply the credit and send a credit memo that shows the VAT adjustment (we’ll need it for our AP records). Also, can you confirm the credit will be visible on the Dec statement and will reduce the payable balance for Nov?

A 30-minute call would be helpful to review the recommendations on idempotency keys. Can you share availability?

Thanks —
Laura
Accounts Payable | Acme Corp
